card.name: Comma after "If ... occurs" warnings
card.fires_on: The comma that closes an "If [problem] occurs" clause in warnings about superinfection or hypersensitivity, just before the instruction to stop the drug. It also fires weakly on spaces inside dosing-table grids and on "to" after "ability" or "potential".

modes.label: Comma after if-occurs clause
modes.description: The comma after a conditional clause such as "If superinfection occurs", right before the instruction to discontinue or contact a physician.
modes.example: If superinfection occurs<<,>> the antibacterial should be discontinued and appropriate

modes.label: Gaps in dose tables
modes.description: A space or repeated unit inside a table of doses, volumes and 0/1 entries.

modes.label: "to" before an action
modes.description: The word "to" after a noun like ability or potential, leading into a verb of what to do.
modes.example: which may impair the ability<< to>> drive a car or operate machinery.

card.plain: It marks the point in a warning where the text turns from "if this happens" to "then do this".
